definition: Small bottleneck modules inserted between transformer layers and trained while the base stays frozen.
details: Small bottleneck modules inserted between transformer layers and trained while the base stays frozen. The original PEFT approach; largely superseded by LoRA but conceptually foundational.

explainer.lead: Adapters let a large transformer learn a new task by training only small modules added between its layers, while the original model stays unchanged. This makes adaptation much lighter than retraining the whole model and established a foundational approach to parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a big, complicated machine that you are not allowed to open or change. You can teach it a new job by plugging a few small attachments between its parts and teaching only those attachments. The main machine stays the same, and you can train different attachments for different jobs.
tiers.practitioner: Insert bottleneck adapters between transformer layers, freeze every base-model parameter, and optimize only the adapter weights on the target task. Adapters are conceptually useful for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, although LoRA has largely superseded them in practice.
tiers.paperLevel: Let theta denote the frozen base-transformer parameters and phi the parameters of bottleneck modules inserted between its layers. Training solves min_phi L(F_{theta,phi}(x), y), keeping theta fixed and updating only phi. The base model therefore cannot adapt its own weights, and this original PEFT approach has largely been superseded by LoRA.

explainer.example: To adapt a pretrained transformer for support-ticket classification, insert adapters between its layers and train on labeled tickets. The transformer's original weights never change; only the adapters learn to produce useful ticket-category predictions.

usedIn.name: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
usedIn.detail: Adapters are the original approach of training small added modules instead of the full model.

usedIn.name: Transformer model adaptation
usedIn.detail: Bottleneck modules are placed between transformer layers to adapt a frozen base to a target task.

explainer.intuition: Instead of rewriting all of a transformer's knowledge for each new task, leave it intact and learn a small amount of task-specific circuitry. The narrow bottleneck keeps the added module small.
howItWorks: Insert small bottleneck modules between its layers.
Run task data through the adapted model.
explainer.whyItMatters: Adapters showed that a transformer could be adapted without training all of its parameters. They laid the conceptual groundwork for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, even though LoRA has largely taken their place.
misconceptions: Adapters do not fine-tune the base model; its weights remain frozen.
The bottleneck modules are trained, not the entire transformer.
Adapters and LoRA are related PEFT ideas, but they are not the same method.

nodes.label: Bottleneck adapter
nodes.note: Only these small modules are trained.
